description:
Port-map §4. Pure function. Takes a complete byte sequence from
StdinFSM and returns {:key, %Key{}} or {:char, bin} or
:paste_start/:paste_end or :unknown.

- OctoPi.Tui.KeyParser.parse/1 — multi-head pattern matching on
  binary shape (Kitty CSI-u / legacy ESC-prefix / printable ASCII
  / printable Unicode / fallback). NO top-level cond.
- OctoPi.Tui.Key struct: {key, modifiers, event_type}.
- Legacy table as a @module attribute map: "\e[A" → {:key, :up},
  etc. Full set: arrows, F1-F12, Home, End, PgUp/Dn, Insert,
  Delete, paste-start/end, Shift/Ctrl/Alt variants.
- Kitty CSI-u: parse "\e[<code>[;<mod>[:<event>]]u", translate
  modifier bitmask (shift=1, alt=2, ctrl=4, super=8, stored as
  mod-1), decode event_type (press/repeat/release).

Mirrors upstream keys.ts (1,100+ LOC TS) → ~300 LOC Elixir thanks
to pattern matching. Tests lift from port-map §14.2 (keys.test.ts,
615 lines).

TDD:
- Pure function, no I/O, no state — pure unit tests.
- Cover every case in §14.2: alternate layouts (Cyrillic, Dvorak),
  keypad, event types, shifted keys, modifyOtherKeys, legacy
  Ctrl+letter, Alt-prefix, arrows CSI+SS3, F1-F12, env-aware
  (SSH_CONNECTION, WT_SESSION).

Depends on .1.
title: Key parser: CSI-u + legacy + printable → %Key{}
